title: Fixed-parameter estimates and growing-parameter uniformity
pvg_object: a family of valuation observables or regions indexed by q, r, support depth, or truncation scale
ant_object: parameter-explicit constants, domains, conductors, and error terms in an analytic estimate
forward_translation: Every geometric parameter must be propagated into local factors, continuation margins, vertical bounds, residues, and the final implied constant.
reverse_translation: A theorem uniform in a parameter yields a family-level geometric statement only over the explicitly certified range; fixed-parameter estimates do not determine such a range.
preserved_information: which parameters are fixed, which vary, and where each dependence enters the proof
lost_information: hidden big-O dependence cannot be reconstructed after constants have been suppressed
trigger: A fixed-q, fixed-r, or fixed-depth argument is proposed for parameters growing with x.
typical_output: an explicit admissible parameter range or a named uniformity obstruction
error_or_wall: Compact-set or fixed-conductor estimates may deteriorate with the parameter and destroy the shifted contour or remainder.
required_certificate: List every varying parameter, quantify all local and vertical constants, and prove the claimed range survives summation and contour transfer.
positive_example: A fixed-r residual bound is upgraded only after its O_r constant and half-plane margin are controlled uniformly for r in the stated range.
counterexample: An estimate O_{q,r}(x^a) gives no information when q or r grows with x.
anti_overclaim: Never erase a subscript from an implied constant when promoting a fixed-parameter theorem.
classification: Uniformity gate / no automatic family theorem
source_basis: Standard parameter-uniformity discipline in analytic number theory

title: General-theorem subsumption and novelty classification
pvg_object: a newly defined valuation observable with an apparently new analytic consequence
ant_object: a parameterized published theorem whose hypotheses may already imply the consequence
forward_translation: Before claiming a new theorem, map every local factor, regularity assumption, parameter range, and error term into the nearest general framework.
reverse_translation: A general theorem can certify the analytic consequence but does not determine whether the observable, formulation, or application is significant.
preserved_information: logical implication and exact parameter matching
lost_information: methodological novelty and significance are not created by instantiation
trigger: The proof becomes routine after defining the observable or cites a standard Selberg--Delange, Wirsing, or Tauberian framework.
typical_output: known corollary, new application, modest new theorem, or unresolved subsumption
error_or_wall: Name changes and geometric motivation can obscure that the analytic statement is already covered.
required_certificate: Provide exact source attribution and a line-by-line hypothesis and conclusion comparison, including constants and parameter uniformity.
positive_example: A factorization falling directly under a published Selberg--Delange theorem is at most a new application unless an uncovered feature is proved.
counterexample: Absence of an identical title or notation is not evidence of originality.
anti_overclaim: Correct instantiation of a known theorem is not a new analytic method.
